Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 20-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Generative AI and Large Language Models [NPT_4121]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                   Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Evaluate how the properties of word embeddings contribute to downstream NLP model                   (5)  
  performance. Compare traditional one-hot encoding with embedding-based representations and  
  A)           justify why embeddings outperform them in semantic understanding.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Apply your understanding of the NLP pipeline to explain how raw text is transformed into model-     (3)  
  ready input. Identify any three key stages and describe their purpose briefly.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           During the training of a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) for predicting stock prices, the model      (2)  
  struggles to learn long-term dependencies in the data. As an ML engineer, you are asked to  
  suggest an appropriate training method to improve the model's learning process.  
  Analyze the purpose of Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT) in training RNNs and demonstrate  
  how it helps the model capture temporal dependencies in sequential data.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Assess how Embeddings from Language Model (ELMo) differ from static embeddings like                 (5)  
  Word2Vec or GloVe. Evaluate ELMo's advantages in representing contextual meaning and its  
  A)           impact on NLP model performance.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Examine how BERT's bidirectional attention mechanism enables better understanding of context (3)  
  compared to unidirectional models like GPT.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Use your understanding of Large Language Models (LLMs) to illustrate two major characteristics      (2)  
  that set them apart from traditional NLP systems and show how these characteristics enhance  
  real-world language processing tasks.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)                Critically analyze how identifying the right use case influences the success of a Generative AI     (5)  
  project. Propose criteria for evaluating whether a use case is suitable for generative modeling.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  Page #1

B)          Apply the concept of Representation Learning to explain how deep neural networks automatically (3)  
  extract useful features from raw data, reducing manual feature engineering.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)          Apply your understanding of Foundation Models to identify three major models that have advanced (2)  
  the field of Artificial Intelligence and explain how each has contributed to practical AI innovations.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)               Design an experiment using OpenAI Playground to evaluate the emergent abilities of a                  (5)  
  Transformer-based Large Language Model. Discuss how you would measure performance and  
  A)          interpret results.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)          Examine how Prompt Engineering (PE) enhances the output quality of Generative AI models.              (3)  
  Explain using an example of rewriting prompts for better accuracy.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)          Use your understanding of text generation techniques to differentiate between Top-k and Top-p         (2)  
  (nucleus) sampling and illustrate how each method influences the diversity and coherence of  
  generated text.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5)               Evaluate the architectural design of Generative Pre-trained Models (GPT-like) and justify how         (5)  
  pre-training and fine-tuning stages together enable state-of-the-art text generation capabilities.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)          Demonstrate how AI agents that can use tools (e.g., calculators, search APIs, or code interpreters) (3)  
  enhance the performance of Large Language Models in real-world applications. Provide one  
  example.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)          Apply your understanding of Natural Language Processing (NLP) to describe two fundamental             (2)  
  goals of NLP in Artificial Intelligence and demonstrate how these goals are achieved through real-  
  world applications.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  
  -----End-----
